sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text: Castelnau-le-Lez, on the eastern edge of Montpellier, has moved its centre from paid street parking to a free time-limited blue zone. The town's pages describe a two-hour limit with a disc, 8am to 8pm, with a 35 euro fine; the two pages disagree on whether it applies on Saturdays, and both use the future tense, so neither gives a start date, although a town page of August 2026 treats the limit as existing. The stated aims are more turnover for shops, fewer long-stay cars and easier parking for residents [0]. The blue-zone page says the four pay-and-display machines in the centre are to be removed by TaM in a first phase [1]. On 21 August 2026 the town announced a sticker for shopkeepers and professionals with a local in the town, exempting them from the time limit, with two stickers per business, renewable each year [2]. Castelnau was one of the 11 communes in the first phase of the metropolitan low-emission zone, with all 31 planned from 1 July 2026, but whether the extension took effect was not confirmed [15]. A press report of February 2025 said mayors had agreed to treat the zone as dormant, with no fines until 2027; the council vote was still to come then, and we did not verify later developments [16].

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text: The development story is the Sablassou hub on tram line 2. A TaM leaflet of May 2025 announced bustram line A from 23 May 2025 between Place de l'Europe and Notre-Dame de Sablassou, with 8 stations, 16 minutes and a bus every ten minutes in the daytime, and an extension to Castries via Le Crès and Vendargues planned for 2028; residents of those towns are invited to park at Sablassou [11]. The town's 2024 mobility map shows a bustram station and a TER station, with a target of 2030, still to come; it is a target, not a decision [13]. In July 2024 the town announced charge points at the Palais des Sports, on avenue Georges-Frêche, at the two P+Tram sites and at the Charles-de-Gaulle car park; the article uses the future tense and gives no installation dates [14]. The metropolitan open-data portal has a Castelnau car-park dataset, but it is a weekly map extract, not live availability [17].

sections.title: Operators, positioning and utilisation
sections.text:
Three free long-stay car parks are listed, Jules Ferry (20 spaces), Rose de France (130) and Des écoles (80). The blue-zone page adds two car parks near tram stations, the stade (50) and the Centurions (100), without saying what they cost [3]. Le Vicarello, a public underground car park of 64 spaces, is paid from 7am to noon and 2pm to 8pm, with two free hours per half-day, and is free at midday, on Sundays and after 8pm [4]. TaM runs two P+Tram sites. Notre-Dame de Sablassou has 350 spaces on the route de Nîmes, and other sources give 379, which we could not reconcile [5]; residents living nearby can subscribe for 20 euros a month for evenings, nights and weekends [6]. At Charles de Gaulle the town lists 200 spaces, and the price grid it refers to is not displayed on the page [7]. Holders of a TaM card or a Pass gratuité park free for up to 24 hours when they continue by public transport [12][8]. Tram line 2 has stopped at eight stations in the commune since 2006, and the town says Place de la Comédie is under 15 minutes away [9].

Our data cover three car parks, measured since 5 October 2026 (17 days) and fewer for Charles de Gaulle. Sablassou (350 spaces) averaged about 44% on weekdays and 29% at weekends, with a peak of 85% on a Thursday afternoon. Le Vicarello (64) averaged 44% on weekdays and 24% at weekends, peaking at 86% on a Tuesday morning. Charles de Gaulle, which our feed lists with 50 spaces, averaged 33% on weekdays and 2% at weekends over 9 days, peaking at 76% on a Thursday morning. These are short series.
